papers.title: Sex-Related Differences in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Primary Mitral Regurgitation
papers.short_title: sex differences after edge-to-edge repair for primary mitral regurgitation
papers.summary: No abstract is available for this paper yet, so no results are reported here. Written by Pezzola, Serafini, Ludwig, Patel, Stolz, Tanaka, Trenkwalder and colleagues, it compares women and men undergoing mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for primary, degenerative mitral regurgitation, looking at baseline characteristics, procedural results and clinical outcomes by sex. Its author list overlaps with the international PRIME-MR registry group. See the full paper for findings.
papers.critique: Without an abstract, only the question and likely design can be judged. Best: sex-specific data after edge-to-edge repair for primary regurgitation are scarce, and women have historically done worse after surgical mitral repair, so a large multicentre analysis is welcome. Weakest: it is likely observational, so confounding and selection, such as surgery being withheld for age or frailty, limit causal conclusions. For context, a related PRIME-MR conference abstract at the 2026 German Cardiac Society meeting reported 2078 patients, higher gradients and more residual regurgitation in women, yet lower two-year all-cause mortality, hazard ratio 0.67; the published figures may differ. No independent commentary on this paper was found yet.

papers.title: Right-Ventricular Damage and Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation
papers.short_title: right ventricular damage in severe tricuspid regurgitation
papers.summary: No abstract is available for this paper yet, so no results are reported here. From Brunner, Kalbacher, Wild, Kessler, Rudolph, Lurz, Thiele, Hausleiter and colleagues, a group behind the European tricuspid registries, it examines how the degree of right ventricular damage relates to clinical outcomes in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation, a central question when deciding whether and when to offer transcatheter tricuspid therapy. See the full paper for findings.
papers.critique: Without an abstract, only the question can be judged. Best: right ventricular function is the key unknown in timing tricuspid intervention, and this group has large multicentre datasets; their 2025 EuroTR analysis in this journal, of 2191 patients after tricuspid edge-to-edge repair, found that lower TAPSE, a larger right ventricle and residual regurgitation each predicted mortality, with the worst outcomes when dysfunction and dilation coexisted. Weakest: echo measures of the right ventricle are load dependent and vary between readers, observational data cannot show that earlier treatment reverses damage, and treatment choice may confound outcomes. No independent commentary on this paper was found yet.

critique_sources.title: The Relevance of Right Ventricular Function and Dimension in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair

papers.title: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection: implications for women's health, clinical care, and future research.
papers.short_title: a review of spontaneous coronary artery dissection
papers.summary: This Lancet Review by Bay, Magnussen, Adlam and colleagues summarises evidence on spontaneous coronary artery dissection, an increasingly recognised cause of acute coronary syndromes that mainly affects younger women and is more common than once thought. Early adverse-event risk is substantial, particularly in the first weeks. Because dissections often heal spontaneously, conservative management is preferred, with revascularisation reserved for ongoing ischaemia or haemodynamic compromise. It also covers genetics, diagnosis, reproductive health and research priorities.
papers.relevance: Directly relevant to the cath lab: a useful update on recognising SCAD at angiography and on when to resist stenting.

papers.title: Lipid-Lowering Strategies in the Era of Early Atherosclerosis Detection: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement
papers.short_title: the 2026 ACC statement on earlier lipid lowering
papers.summary: This 2026 American College of Cardiology Scientific Statement, chaired by Philip Greenland, reviews the case for earlier and more sustained lipid lowering, since atherosclerosis begins early and is driven by cumulative LDL exposure. It covers lifetime lipid burden, risk enhancers and imaging of subclinical atherosclerosis, which may reveal risk underestimated by calculators. Direct trial evidence in young, low-risk people is limited, so it advises individualised, shared decisions integrating short- and long-term risk.
papers.study_type: ACC scientific statement (abstract from publisher page)
papers.relevance: Useful background when advising relatives of young coronary patients or acting on plaque seen incidentally on CT, though it reflects American rather than ESC practice.
